newsitem.title: BELGIUM: KREDIETBANK SLIPS AS MERGER TALK FADES.
newsitem.headline: KREDIETBANK SLIPS AS MERGER TALK FADES.

text.p: Shares in third largest Belgian bank Kredietbank lost 1.36 percent on a weaker Brussels bourse as the bank re-affirmed in a newspaper interview that it would prefer to remain independent, quashing merger speculation.
The stock was down 250 francs at 14,500 francs at 0930 GMT, continuing to slide from its June 9 peak of 16,200.
"The share had risen quite a lot recently as a result of the speculation," a trader said. Looking at recent trends, the share could find technical support in 14,400 to 14,200 franc area.
The share's loss on Wednesday compared with a 0.67 percent drop by the Bel-20 share index, down 15 points at 2,344 at 0940 GMT following a correction from a rapid, recent rise.

Kredietbank's slippage was exacerbated by chief executive officer Marcel Cockaerts' comments in an interview, stressing that he was bent on bucking what he called a recent fad in the industry towards mergers and takeovers.

"We have a nice future ahead of us and we don't want to jeopardise that for something fashionable," he was quoted as telling Belgian financial daily De Financieel-Economische Tijd. "Kredietbank is not in a situation where it must do something."
"The bank is stressing its independence, which means a deal with Rabobank and Cera is being postponed," a trader said.
Kredietbank said last month it was in what it called exploratory talks with Rabobank, a Dutch cooperative bank, and Belgium's Cera Bank.

"Cockaerts is negating that a merger is in the pipeline. We will probably have to wait for his successor next year (before there is a chance of a merger). Cockaerts is rather conservative, he does not like fads," the trader added.
He said the share was still expensive, even at current levels. Instead, players should buy Dexia bank stock.
Dexia was holding up relatively well on the weaker market, trading up five francs at 3,910.
Traders said Kredietbank was also facing selling pressure after a downgrade by Merrill Lynch. The brokerage recommended investing in the holding company behind Kredietbank, Almanij, instead.
Almanij shares bucked the trend of the 20 blue chip stocks, trading up 150 francs at 16,550.
